title: Nepal Lion:
headline: A Lion from Nepal served his country through the 2015 earthquake, and now he is glad to meet Lions from every country.
story: Raju opens with where he is from: Nepal, country of Everest. In 2015 a great earthquake hit Nepal, and he is very proud that he served at that time. He chose Lions to be part of the largest helping organization.

The tie-back is friendship: to meet Lions from different countries, he is very glad and very happy. His English is simple and slow. Cut the pauses, keep his words. Warm and proud, never sad about the earthquake.
do: Open on frame 1 with his line <q>I belongs to Nepal, country of Everest.</q> Big captions.
Cut his long pauses hard. He speaks slowly; the cut must not.
Keep the earthquake to one line plus his pride.
Keep his Nepali cap and the Nepal flag pin in frame. They are the visual hook.
End on <q>I'm very glad and very happy.</q>
dont: No logo, title or name card at 0:00. No “Hi, my name is Raju Khadka” intro.
Don't correct his grammar in the captions. Caption what he says.
No earthquake footage, no stock, no sad music.
Don't use IMG_7894 (Atdhe's “four friends in Nepal” line) or the other Lions in IMG_8044–8047.

client_note: Why this matters: Hong Kong cuts lead with friendship, and this interview is mostly service. His one singular story is the 2015 earthquake, and he ends glad to meet Lions from every country. Ledger tag: SPECIFIC-SCENE, sub-angle “served his own country in the 2015 earthquake” (New York is a hotel lobby, Philippines is a new Lion welcomed). Runners-up: “Since our motto is We Sharp [We Serve], we are born to serve. So all lions from the world, I request you all to be the part of service.” (IMG_7893 01:03.50–01:18.40, alternative button); “I am in this moment lines moment since 2009” (IMG_7885 ≈00:30.8–00:37.4, check the words by ear).
